catalog_quote: The tentative investigation into the acoustic correlates of lexical accent in Dolgan already implies that the latter tends to be realized on the last syllable of a word form. However, this is not without exceptions. ... In bare stems, the lexical accent falls, as a rule, on the last syllable of the stem. ... As can be seen from the list, the last syllable of a bare nominal or verbal stem is, per default, accented, regardless of either word and syllable structure or long vowels in non-final syllables. Coming to adjectives, pronouns and adverbs, there are, however, some exceptions from this pattern. When the emphatic prefix h- is attached to a demonstrative pro-form or adverb, the lexical accent falls on the word’s first syllable. ... When suffixes are added to a stem, the lexical accent is usually shifted to the attached suffix. If more than one suffix is attached, the syllable corresponding to the last suffix of the word form is accented. This can be illustrated by the following accent patterns of ogo ‘child’ and bar- ‘go’. ... ogó ‘child’ ogo-lór ‘child-pl’ ogo-lor-bút ‘child-pl-poss.1pl’ ogo-lor-butu-gár ‘child-pl-poss.1pl-dat/loc’ bár ‘go’ bar-ár ‘go-prs.3sg’ bar-d-á ‘go-pst1-3sg’ bar-dɨ-bɨ́t ‘go-pst1-1pl’ bar-dag-ɨná ‘go-cond/temp-3sg’ bar-dak-pɨtɨná ‘go-cond/temp-1pl’

new_statements.quote: Долганское ударение падает, как правило, на последний слог слова; при присоединении суффиксов ударение перемещается в конец. Есть два исключения: слова, образованные с помощью эмфатического префикса һ- (һонон «именно так» онон «так»), и слова, образованные из двух корней (һарсиэрда «утро, утром» һарсын «завтра» + эрдэ «рано»).
new_statements.translation: Dolgan stress falls, as a rule, on the last syllable of the word; when suffixes are attached the stress moves to the end. There are two exceptions: words formed with the emphatic prefix һ- (һонон 'exactly so' ← онон 'so'), and words formed from two roots (һарсиэрда 'morning, in the morning' ← һарсын 'tomorrow' + эрдэ 'early').

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is on the final syllable of the (suffixed) word; it shifts rightward as suffixes are added. Exceptions: forms with the emphatic prefix һ- and two-root compounds, where stress does not fall on the final syllable (the text does not say which syllable carries it in these cases).
new_statements.exceptions: Two: (1) words with the emphatic prefix һ- (һонон < онон); (2) two-root compounds (һарсиэрда < һарсын + эрдэ). Position of stress in these exceptions is not stated.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (stress moves to the end of the suffixed word). Source is a popular-science web longread written by the INEL Dolgan team (including the author of the 2022 Brill grammar), not an academic publication; it should be superseded by Däbritz 2022 ch. 2 when accessible.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes Dolgan in general (Taimyr; both Upper and Lower dialects). Ubrjatova 1985 (list of works to obtain) describes specifically the Noril'sk variety (no separate glottocode found; falls under dolg1241). Two of the eight Glottolog 'descriptive' refs are misattributed to Dolgan (Schmidt 2011 is a review of an Old Irish textbook; Aks'onova 1987 is on Bantu noun classes).

sources.note: Word stress falls as a rule on the last syllable of the word; when suffixes are added the stress moves to the end; two exceptions: words formed with the emphatic prefix һ- (һонон 'именно так' < онон 'так') and words formed from two roots (һарсиэрда 'morning' < һарсын 'tomorrow' + эрдэ 'early'). Authors are the INEL Dolgan team (Däbritz wrote the 2022 Brill grammar).
